title: When Deduplication Reveals Too Much
description: A sync service skips upload whenever a chunk hash exists anywhere in storage. A client can submit a known file's hashes and observe which uploads are skipped. What tradeoff needs attention?

options.text: Global deduplication can reveal file existence; scope deduplication to a user or tenant when that privacy boundary matters.
options.explanation: The skip signal can expose whether another user has particular bytes. Tenant-scoped dedup sacrifices some storage savings to avoid that cross-user signal.

options.text: SHA-256 makes the existence signal private automatically.
options.explanation: A client with candidate bytes can compute their hashes; collision resistance does not hide an observable upload decision.

options.text: Longer upload URLs remove the information leak.
options.explanation: URL lifetime does not change whether the service reveals that a hash already exists.

options.text: Delete chunks whenever any one user's reference disappears.
options.explanation: Other references or in-flight uploads may still need the chunk. Garbage collection must account for them.
